SMTO-CFG-0075 — A Redaction switch has a value that isn't simply on or off

GUID: b8748803-c3a4-4cd0-8a03-2351cdea1191
Slug: redaction-setting-invalid
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • Redaction hides passwords, tokens and similar secrets in logs, activity and other places SMTO shows them. One of its switches has a saved value that isn't plainly on or off, so SMTO stopped rather than guess.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Security › Redaction. For each switch, move it once and back again so it ends where you want it. Using the switch saves a clean on or off value in place of the bad one.
  2. If a script or another program sends tasks or settings to SMTO, ask the person who set it up to send each redaction choice as true or false. Words like "yes" or numbers aren't accepted as on or off.
  3. Then try your action again. If it was a task, first open the conversation and check whether it already started. Checking first avoids running the same work twice.

What success looks like

  • The Redaction section saves without an error, and new tasks start without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; only they can change shared settings if Settings won't let you. Don't turn off other security or permission settings to get past this; they aren't related.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • RedactionPolicy construction failed: the policy input is not a mapping, or a redaction_*_enabled flag is not an exact boolean.

What this means

  • Redaction policy input is not a mapping or any per-source flag is not an exact boolean. The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.

Why this can happen

  • Redaction policy input is not a mapping or any per-source flag is not an exact boolean.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect supported per-source keys and boolean types; diagnostic sanitization is an independent mandatory boundary.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the agent_settings keys redaction_*_enabled and any redaction policy captured in the task submission or Gateway runtime policy; replace non-boolean values (strings, 0/1, null) with true or false, preferably by saving through Settings › Security › Redaction. Mandatory error sanitization is unaffected by these optional switches.
  • Use true or false for each supported redaction switch. Error diagnostics always apply their mandatory sanitizer independently of these optional display settings.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The optional policy validates without changing mandatory error sanitization.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
